findings.evidence: Third pass added two independent Class 3 accounts: a guide service's itinerary ('3rd class rock scrambling up to the very exposed summit pinnacle', after a first loose rock step near 10,500 ft where guides belay) and a personal trip report (the loose notch to the summit, 'class 3'). Both are on the Fryingpan/Whitman side, which shares the summit rock with this route above the Ingraham-Whitman saddle. A Muir/Cowlitz/Ingraham trip report (this exact approach) gives no class but reached the summit unroped in ski boots. Tally now: Class 3 - route database, 100-peaks guide, Lemke, guide itinerary, Eric's Base Camp (5 independent); Class 3-4 - one ski report (a second 'Class 3-4' site, summitborn, looks like an aggregator and is not counted); Class 4 - the club South Face route page, one Summerland-side report, and one report that climbed an alternative line right of a snow-filled gully and called it 'harder than the normal gully... class 4'. Class 3 is now a clear majority for the summit. Caveat: the only source describing this route's specific saddle exit gives it a Class 4 move or two; the stored pitch_detail already says so.

grade.evidence: Five independent accounts rate the summit rock Class 3 (route database '3rd, Steep Snow'; guide itinerary; 100-peaks guide; two trip reports) against one Class 3-4 and three Class 4 (one of those on a non-standard variation). Human reviewer: the South Face saddle exit has a Class 4 move per the one source that describes it; if the grade should cover the worst move on this specific line, 'Class 3-4, steep snow' is the conservative alternative.
